papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on testing whether an unknown quantum Hamiltonian is k-local, with an operator-norm hardness result, an efficient tester under the normalized Frobenius norm, and a hardness result for learning.

assertions.value: The authors state that they establish hardness of Hamiltonian locality testing when distance is measured by the operator norm, and give an efficient locality tester when distance is measured by the normalized Frobenius norm.
quotes: On the one hand, we establish hardness of locality testing with the distance measured by the operator norm. On the other hand, for the normalized Frobenius norm as distance measure, we give an efficient Hamiltonian locality tester.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 (formal: Corollary 4.3), Section 1.2
assertions.reader_inference: Exact query counts and times are in symbols that pdftotext does not render faithfully, so they are left out of the value.

assertions.value: The authors state that they prove learning a general Hamiltonian remains exponentially hard with the average-case (normalized Frobenius) distance.
quotes: Finally, we prove that learning a general Hamiltonian remains exponentially hard with this average-case distance
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1.4 (formal: Theorem 5.1)
assertions.reader_inference: This is the stated basis for the testing versus learning separation.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not assume access to inverse time evolution.
quotes: We note that we do not assume access to inverse time evolution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Footnote 1 states the access model of the paper

papers.what_it_is: An empirical evaluation of two implementations of the hybrid algorithm Quantum Annealing Learning Search (QALS) on a D-Wave annealer, on number partitioning and travelling salesman instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the number partitioning problem the classical exact algorithm outperforms both QALS and the D-Wave Hybrid procedure, and they state that quantum annealing and QALS are not of any practical use for this problem.
quotes: The results obtained on NPP show that quantum annealing, in general, and QALS, in particular, are not of any practical use in this case.
the classical exact algorithm used for NPP outperforms both QALS and Hybrid
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one problem class, Section 6

assertions.value: The authors report that QALS processes travelling salesman problems of higher size than the Embedding Composite procedure used to map the problem to the topology.
quotes: QALS is able to process problems with a higher size than the Embedding Composite procedure used to map the problem to the topology
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, Section 6

assertions.value: The authors state that the two implementations are in C++ and Python, run on the D-Wave machine, and are compared with the Hybrid procedure of the D-Wave suite as a baseline.
quotes: The two implementations are in C++ and Python, respectively and they run on the D-Wave machine.
As a baseline, we compared the results with the Hybrid procedure available in the D-wave suite.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states the setup of the study

assertions.value: The authors state that both QALS and Embedding Composite do not directly provide a valid solution on the travelling salesman problem, and the solution has to be manipulated to become valid.
quotes: However, both QALS and EC do not directly provide a valid solution; indeed, the solution has to be manipulated in order to become valid for the problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 6 states this as a limit of both methods

papers.title_in_file: Solvable Quantum Circuits in Tree+1 Dimensions
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Concluding Remarks; derivations not read.
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that builds exactly solvable quantum circuit dynamics on tree graphs ('tree-unitarity'), generalizing dual-unitary circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that they introduce a family of gates on trees for which the dynamics is exactly solvable, and that imposing tree-unitarity lifts much of the solvability of dual-unitary circuits to trees.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Section VII, pp.1 and 22
quotes: We then introduce a family of gates for which the dynamics is exactly solvable
Imposing tree-unitarity in turn allowed us to lift much of the solvability of dual-unitary circuits to trees.
assertions.certainty_reason: Sections III and IV derive the solvability analytically
assertions.reader_inference: The paper is analytic; the reader did not check the derivations.

assertions.value: The authors state a trade-off between maximal butterfly velocity and non-vanishing correlation functions in tree-unitary models.
quotes: the trade-off between maximal butterfly velocity and non-vanishing correlation functions
assertions.certainty_reason: Sections IV B, V and VI

assertions.value: The authors state that they consider only the setting where the spacelike direction is a tree, with time as the extra non-tree dimension.
quotes: In contrast, here we exclusively consider the setting where only the spacelike direction is a tree
assertions.certainty_reason: Section I states the scope

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section III properties (Property 2), Section IV numerics intro, Section V start, Section VI.
papers.what_it_is: A proposal of the multiple-triangle ansatz (MuTA), a quantum neural network native to measurement-based quantum computing, with numerical demonstrations.

assertions.value: The authors state that they propose the multiple-triangle ansatz (MuTA), a universal quantum neural network assembled from MBQC neurons, and that Property 2 proves MuTA can represent a universal set of gates.
quotes: We propose the multiple-triangle ansatz (MuTA), a universal quantum neural network assembled from MBQC neurons featuring bias engineering, monotonic expressivity, tunable entanglement, and scalable training.
Property 2 proves that MuTA can represent a universal set of gates.
assertions.certainty_reason: Property 2, Section III

assertions.value: The authors state that they provided numerical evidence for the practical value of MuTA by learning a universal gate set, a quantum state classifier and a quantum instrument.
quotes: provided numerical evidence for the practical value of MuTA by learning a universal gate set, a quantum state classifier, and a quantum instrument.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation results from one study, Section IV
assertions.reader_inference: The reader saw no hardware run; the paper's code is a Python simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the hardware-constrained part of the paper they focus on photonic GKP computation.
quotes: Here, we focus on photonic GKP computation
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V states the scope

papers.title_in_file: Quantum circuit complexity and unsupervised machine learning of topological order
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, theorem statements, numerical results section, Discussion; proofs in the supplement not read.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that links Nielsen's quantum circuit complexity to Bures and entanglement distances and uses them as kernels for unsupervised manifold learning of topological phases.

assertions.value: The authors state that Theorems 1 and 2 lead to approximate substitutes of the quantum circuit complexity, namely the Bures distance (fidelity change) and the entanglement-entropy distance.
quotes: Theorems 1 and 2 lead to approximate substitutes of the QCC, i.e., the Bures distance (fidelity change) and the entanglement-entropy distance, respectively
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorems 1 and 2, proofs in the Supplementary Information

assertions.value: The authors report that unsupervised learning on the bond-alternating XXZ chain produces distinct clusters associated with three phases, in good agreement with independent calculations of topological invariants.
quotes: we find that the unsupervised learning produces distinct clusters that can be associated with three phases (trivial, symmetry broken, and topological), in good agreement with independent calculations of topological invariants
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on one model from one study

assertions.value: The authors report that the entanglement-based approach is more robust to local Haar random noises.
quotes: Moreover, we find that the entanglement-based approach, which captures the long-range structure of quantum entanglement of topological orders, is more robust to local Haar random noises.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study

assertions.value: The paper states Theorem 2 for the circuit complexity of a geometrically local quantum circuit with respect to the qubit chain.
quotes: with a geometrically local quantum circuit (with respect to the n-qubit chain) is lower bounded by
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2 statement

papers.title_in_file: Optimal Number-Conserved Linear Encoding for Practical Fermionic Simulation
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2309.09370 v3 (22 Sep 2025); its title differs from the file name (the v1 title) and from the record id ('particle-conserved'), but it is the same arXiv paper.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion, numerical results and limitation passages.
papers.what_it_is: A paper on number-conserved qubit encodings for fermionic simulation using classical parity check codes and a Fermionic Expectation Decoder, tested with VQE on small molecules.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate optimal encoding with a random classical parity check code and propose the Fermionic Expectation Decoder for scalable probability decoding.
quotes: We demonstrate optimal encoding with random classical parity check code and propose the Fermionic Expectation Decoder for scalable probability decoding
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' claim in the abstract; the decoder complexity figure is a symbol the extraction drops

assertions.value: The authors state that the protocol is tested with the variational quantum eigensolver on LiH in the STO-3G and 6-31G basis, and on the H2 potential energy curve in the 6-311G* basis.
quotes: The protocol is tested with variational quantum eigensolver on LiH in the STO-3G and 6-31G basis, and H2 potential energy curve in the 6-311G* basis.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the test setup

assertions.value: The authors state that it remains unexplored whether the RLE-FED protocol can facilitate the scalable implementation of VQE in the compressed subspace.
quotes: it remains unexplored whether the RLE-FED protocol can facilitate the scalable implementation of VQE in the compressed subspace.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this as a limit of their demonstration

assertions.value: The authors report that for the larger LiH system the Hardware-Efficient Ansatz applied directly to the uncompressed Hilbert space starts exhibiting Barren Plateaus.
quotes: However, when scaling up to the (16,2) LiH system, the Hardware-Efficient Ansatz (HEA) applied directly to the uncompressed Hilbert space starts exhibiting Barren Plateaus.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study

papers.title_in_file: Photonic probabilistic machine learning using quantum vacuum noise
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Results on MNIST inference and generation, Discussion.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental photonic probabilistic computer that uses quantum vacuum noise in an optical parametric oscillator as the random source for MNIST classification and generation.

assertions.value: The authors state that their photonic probabilistic neuron is implemented in a bistable optical parametric oscillator with vacuum-level injected bias fields.
quotes: Our PPN is implemented in a bistable optical parametric oscillator (OPO) with vacuum-level injected bias fields.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract states the hardware setup

assertions.value: The authors report an overall experimental classification accuracy of 96.5% for the optical stochastic binary neural network, against 97.0% in numerical simulation.
quotes: the overall experimental classification accuracy (96.5%) is in close agreement with the accuracy obtained from the numerical simulations (97.0%).
assertions.certainty_reason: Experimental result from one study

assertions.value: The authors state that in their demonstration the speed and energy efficiency were limited by the PPN sampling rate and the data transfer bandwidth between electronic processors and the PPNs.
quotes: PPN sampling rate and data transfer bandwidth between electronic processors and PPNs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Discussion states this as a limit of the demonstration
assertions.reader_inference: The all-optical platform and its estimated rate and energy figures are a proposal, not a measurement.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum tree generator improves QAOA state-of-the-art for the knapsack problem
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Conclusion, and the reachability and benchmark passages.
papers.what_it_is: A QAOA variant (AAM-QAOA with a quantum tree generator) for the 0-1 knapsack problem, benchmarked against Copula-QAOA in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that their method consistently outperforms the Copula-based ansatz in terms of the approximation ratio, on hard benchmark sets with up to 20 knapsack items.
quotes: Our numerical results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms the Copula-based ansatz in terms of the approximation ratio as independent measure.
On hard benchmark sets with up to 20 knapsack items
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study

assertions.value: The authors state that for larger instance sizes both approaches fail to deliver better outcomes than greedily packing items in descending value-to-weight ratio, at least for the considered circuit depths.
quotes: However, for larger instance sizes, both approaches fail to deliver better outcomes than greedily packing items in descending value-to-weight ratio, at least for the considered circuit depths.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study

assertions.value: The authors state that for sufficiently high circuit depths they can prove AAM-QAOA will eventually be able to sample the optimal solution.
quotes: For sufficiently high circuit depths, however, we can prove that AAM-QAOA will eventually be able to sample the optimal solution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V, using the QAOA convergence conditions of Ref. [14, Theorem 12]
